title: Harmless system permission warning
explanation: Windows logs this warning constantly on almost every PC. It's a known, harmless quirk and doesn't affect your computer.
likelyCauses: Built-in Windows components asking for permissions they don't need

title: Your PC turned off unexpectedly
explanation: Your PC shut down without going through a normal shutdown, and it wasn't a blue screen. This usually means it lost power, was held off with the power button, or turned itself off to protect itself.
likelyCauses: Power cut, unplugged cable, or a drained laptop battery
Holding the power button while the PC was frozen
Overheating protection
A failing power supply (if it happens often)

fixes.label: Make sure vents aren't blocked and the PC isn't on a soft surface

title: Your PC keeps turning off by itself
explanation: Your PC has lost power several times this week without a normal shutdown. When this repeats, it often points to overheating or a hardware problem with power.
likelyCauses: Overheating (dust, blocked vents, failing fan)
A failing power supply or laptop battery
Loose power cable or faulty power strip

fixes.label: Clean dust from vents and fans, and keep the PC on a hard surface
Try a different wall socket or power cable

title: Your PC crashed with a blue screen
explanation: Windows hit a serious error and had to restart. A single blue screen can be a one-off; it's worth acting if it happens again.
likelyCauses: A buggy or outdated driver (graphics, Wi-Fi, storage)
A recent update or newly installed hardware
Memory or storage problems (if it repeats)

title: Repeated blue-screen crashes
explanation: Your PC has crashed with a blue screen more than once this week. Repeated crashes usually have one underlying cause that's worth tracking down.
likelyCauses: A faulty or outdated driver
Failing memory (RAM) or storage
Overheating

fixes.label: Uninstall anything installed shortly before the crashes started

title: Your graphics driver stopped and recovered
explanation: Your screen may have flickered or gone black for a moment. Windows restarted the graphics driver to recover. Once is usually harmless.
likelyCauses: A graphics driver glitch
A game or app pushing the graphics card hard

title: Your graphics driver keeps crashing
explanation: The graphics driver has crashed and recovered several times. This often shows up as black screens, flicker, or games closing.
likelyCauses: Outdated or corrupted graphics driver
Graphics card overheating
Unstable overclock

fixes.label: Update your graphics driver from the PC or graphics card maker's website

title: An app closed unexpectedly
explanation: An app crashed and closed. A single crash is usually a one-off bug in that app.
likelyCauses: A bug in the app
Not enough free memory

title: {app} keeps crashing
explanation: The same app has crashed several times today. That usually means something specific is wrong with that app or its settings.
likelyCauses: A bad update of that app
Corrupted app settings or cache
A conflict with another program or plug-in

fixes.label: Restart your PC, then try the app again

title: An app froze
explanation: An app stopped responding for a while. ResMan checks what else was happening at that moment.
likelyCauses: The app was waiting on something slow (disk, network)
The PC was low on memory
Another program was using most of the CPU

title: {app} keeps freezing
explanation: The same app has frozen several times this week. Look at what the PC was doing during those freezes for the pattern.
likelyCauses: Low memory while the app is open
Too many tabs, add-ons, or open files
A background task competing for the disk

fixes.label: Close tabs or files you aren't using

title: Your PC slowed itself down because of heat
explanation: The processor ran slower than normal to stay cool. A little of this is normal under heavy load.
likelyCauses: Heavy work like games or video
Blocked vents or dust
A warm room or a soft surface under a laptop

fixes.label: Keep vents clear and use the laptop on a hard surface

title: Your PC is running hot often
explanation: Your processor has been slowing itself down to stay cool many times today. This makes everything feel slower and can point to a cooling problem.
likelyCauses: Dust build-up in fans or vents
A background app keeping the CPU busy
Aging thermal paste or a failing fan

fixes.label: Use the Balanced power mode instead of Best performance

title: Your drive reported damaged areas
explanation: Your storage drive reported a damaged area it couldn't read. This can be an early sign the drive is failing.
likelyCauses: The drive is wearing out or failing
A loose or faulty cable (desktop PCs)

fixes.label: Back up your important files now

title: Your drive had trouble reading data
explanation: Windows had trouble reading from or writing to a drive. Once can be a glitch; repeated errors suggest a drive or cable problem.
likelyCauses: A failing drive
A loose cable or a USB drive being removed
Power-saving glitches on external drives

title: Your drive was slow to respond
explanation: Windows had to retry reading or writing to a drive several times. This can cause freezes and may be an early warning sign.
likelyCauses: A drive that's starting to fail
Storage driver problems
A very full drive

title: A drive's health is getting worse
explanation: One of your drives is reporting, through its own built-in health checks, that something is wrong: rising errors, heavy wear, or a warning status. Drives often show these signs before they fail.
likelyCauses: The drive is wearing out or starting to fail
Overheating
A loose or faulty cable (desktop PCs)

fixes.label: Back up your important files now

title: Files on your drive may be damaged
explanation: Windows found problems in the way files are organized on a drive. It can usually repair this itself.
likelyCauses: The PC turned off unexpectedly while saving
A failing drive (if it repeats)

fixes.label: Restart your PC so Windows can check and repair the drive

title: Your PC ran out of memory
explanation: Your PC ran so low on memory that Windows had to step in. This often causes freezes and apps closing.
likelyCauses: Too many apps or browser tabs open at once
One app using far more memory than it should

fixes.label: Close apps and browser tabs you aren't using
Turn off apps that start automatically

title: Your hardware reported a corrected error
explanation: Your hardware found and fixed small errors on its own. Occasional ones are fine; lots of them can be an early warning.
likelyCauses: Unstable overclock or memory settings
Aging hardware
A device driver issue

title: Your hardware reported a serious error
explanation: A piece of hardware (often the processor or memory) reported an error it couldn't fix. This is worth getting checked.
likelyCauses: Failing memory, processor, or motherboard
Overheating
Unstable overclock

fixes.label: Undo any overclocking in your PC's settings

title: Your Wi-Fi keeps disconnecting
explanation: Your Wi-Fi connection dropped several times today.
likelyCauses: Weak signal or interference
Wi-Fi adapter power saving
An outdated Wi-Fi driver or router firmware

title: Startup is slow
explanation: Your PC took more than two minutes to start up.
likelyCauses: Too many apps starting automatically
A nearly full or slow drive
Pending Windows updates

fixes.label: Turn off apps that start automatically
